ethics_check.title: Ethics Approval Check
ethics_check.summary_text: All papers that appeared to involve live data collection contained an ethics approval statement.

table.text: PlanetDiet study is conducted in accordance with the principles of the Declaration of Helsinki.

The protocol, the informed consent, the participant information sheet and the recruitment material have undergone ethical review and approval by the "The Ethical Committee of the Capital Region of Denmark", study code: H-25030722 (date of approval: 18/08/2025).
Any use of the stored samples for future clinical trials will require approval from the relevant Ethics Committee.
However, audits and inspections by the relevant authorities, including the Institutional Review Board or Independent Ethics Committee, must be permitted.
table.header: Frequency and plans for auditing trial conduct

table.text: Any important protocol modifications will be submitted to the relevant Research Ethics Committee (VEK) for approval.

Following publication of the main trial results, deidentified participantlevel data, the data dictionary, statistical code, and selected study materials will be made available upon reasonable request, subject to applicable ethical approvals, data protection requirements, and approval by the study investigators.
Ethics approval and consent to participate PLANETDIET: Sustainable diets and cardiometabolic health: a multi-omics approach in a Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT).
The Ethical Committee of the Capital Region Denmark E-Journal-nr.: H-25030722, amendment number 126414.
Ethics Committee's pamphlet by digital letter.
Participants are randomized to a PHD, an ovolacto-vegetarian diet, or their habitual diet (control).

Digital tools, including websites and mobile applications, may facilitate this process by translating dietary recommendations into actionable guidance and providing accesible continous support in daily life, particularly when participants are changing behaviour towards unfamiliar foods and meal patterns 20.
table.formatted: Digital tools, including websites and mobile applications, may facilitate this process by translating dietary recommendations into actionable guidance and providing accesible continous support in daily life, particularly when participants are changing behaviour towards unfamiliar foods and meal patterns <ref type="bibr" target="#b19">20</ref>.

table.text: Inclusion and exclusion criteria of participants Item Inclusion criteria Adults (males and females) between 45 and 70 years of age at the time of inclusion.
Participants are not institutionalized, able to read and provide consent before participation, and willing to attend in-person visits at the study site.
Participants are responsible for preparing their own meals at home.

Participants are attending two group sessions during the intervention period, providing opportunities to ask questions, receive feedback from study staff, and share experiences with other participants in small groups (5-15 individuals).

Participants are instructed not to make any lifestyle changes during the six-month intervention, which includes changes in physical activity or over-the-counter medication (unless instructed by the doctor).
table.header: Concomitant care permitted or prohibited during the trial

table.text: At every subsequent study visit, participants are asked if they have experienced any new medical condition since the last evaluation.
Participants are randomized in a 1:1:1 allocation ratio to one of three groups: PHD, ovo-lacto-vegetarian, or control, through REDCap.
Study participants are assigned a unique study number (study ID) as well as a secondary unique identifier.
Volunteers are informed about their right to compensation if they experience minor or major adverse effects because of the study intervention (patienterstatningen.dk).
During their participation at NEXS facilities, participants are insured by the University of Copenhagen insurance.
Potential participants are encouraged to review the materials carefully and may bring a bystander to the meeting.

power.title: Power Analysis Check

table.text: To ensure a two-sided paired comparison with 5% significance and 80% statistical power, 60 participants per group will be recruited to detect a difference between groups in the metabolic health z-score. This calculation is based on a previous RCT with similar characteristics that reported a significant reduction of 2.5% in the 10-year Framingham Risk Score between a green-Mediterranean diet and a habitual diet after six months. The common SD was 4.5%, and a dropout rate of 20% has been anticipated in our calculations 36.

report: We used the LLM model 'vllm/DeepSeek-V41-Flash-1017-FP8' to check the contents of 1 paragraph that contained words suggesting they might contain power analyses. Some essential information could not be detected: sample_size, effect_size, effect_size_metric, software ```{r} #| echo: false # table data -------------------------------------- table <- structure(list(power_type = "apriori", statistical_test = "other", sample_size = NA_real_, alpha_level = 0.05, power = 0.8, effect_size = NA_real_, effect_size_metric = NA_character_, software = NA_character_), row.names = c(NA, -1L), class = c("tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame")) # display table ----------------------------------- metacheck::report_table(table, "auto", 5, FALSE) ``` ```{r} #| echo: false # table data -------------------------------------- table <- structure(list(text = "To ensure a two-sided paired comparison with 5% significance and 80% statistical power, 60 participants per group will be recruited to detect a difference between groups in the metabolic health z-score. This calculation is based on a previous RCT with similar characteristics that reported a significant reduction of 2.5% in the 10-year Framingham Risk Score between a green-Mediterranean diet and a habitual diet after six months. The common SD was 4.5%, and a dropout rate of 20% has been anticipated in our calculations 36."), row.names = c(NA, -1L), class = c("tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame")) # display table ----------------------------------- metacheck::report_table(table, "auto", 5, FALSE) ``` ::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"} Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size. For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like: > An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group. For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like: > A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5. :::

table.formatted: Statistical significance will be established at a p-value < 0.05 (two-tailed).
table.expanded: Statistical significance will be established at a p-value < 0.05 (two-tailed).

report: Reporting *p* values imprecisely (e.g., *p* < .05) reduces transparency, reproducibility, and re-use (e.g., in *p* value meta-analyses). Best practice is to report exact p-values with three decimal places (e.g., *p* = .032) unless *p* values are smaller than 0.001, in which case you can use *p* < .001.

This module sometimes flags false positives when sentences discuss how p-value thresholds were set. It can also miss an imprecise p-value that is reported against a threshold (e.g., "decreased at the *p* < .05 significance threshold").

```{r}
#| echo: false


# table data --------------------------------------
table <- structure(list("P-Value" = "p-value < 0.05", Text = "Statistical significance will be established at a p-value < 0.05 (two-tailed)."), row.names = c(NA, 
-1L), class = c("tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame"))

# display table -----------------------------------
metacheck::report_table(table, c(0.1, 0.9), 2, FALSE)
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"} The APA manual states: Report exact *p* values (e.g., *p* = .031) to two or three decimal places. However, report *p* values less than .001 as *p* < .001. However, 2 decimals is too imprecise for many use-cases (e.g., a *p* value meta-analysis), so report *p* values with three digits. American Psychological Association (2020). Publication manual of the American Psychological Association, 7 edition. American Psychological Association. :::
